chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ḥammād, from Bakr ibn Karīb, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man performing ghusl from janābah: should he wash his feet after the ghusl? He said: “If he is performing ghusl in a place where the water flows over his feet, then there is no problem if he does not wash them; but if he is performing ghusl in a place where his feet remain standing in the water, then let him wash them.”

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.تَسْتَنْقِعُ: collects or becomes stagnant, referring to pooled water around the feet
key_terms.رِجْلَيْهِ: his two feet, the specific body part discussed in the ruling
key_terms.يَسِيلُ: flows, meaning the water runs off rather than collecting

ai.seo_question: Does a person need to wash his feet after ghusl from janābah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning washing the feet after ghusl from janābah. It explains that if the water flows away from the feet, no separate washing is required, but if the feet remain in pooled water, they should be washed.
